title: Going to the Moon
examples: What did the astronauts wear when they went to the Moon?
How did the rockets get to space?
What is special about the Moon's surface?

explain.say: Today we learn about going to the Moon.
Rockets use powerful engines to push them up.
Astronauts are people trained for space travel.
When astronauts walk on the Moon, they leave footprints.
Apollo 11 was the mission that landed humans on the Moon.
In real life, we use rockets for many things too.

faq.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
faq.a: Neil Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon. He was part of the Apollo 11 mission.
asks: Who walked on the Moon first?
Which astronaut first stepped on the Moon?
Who was the first Moon walker?

faq.a: A spacesuit keeps astronauts alive in the vacuum of space. It provides air and protection from radiation.
asks: Why do astronauts wear big suits?
What keeps astronauts safe in space?
What is the purpose of a spacesuit?

faq.a: Rockets work by burning fuel to create hot gas. This gas pushes the rocket out the back very fast.
asks: What makes a rocket go fast?
How does a rocket get off the ground?

faq.q: Do footprints on the Moon last forever?
faq.a: Yes, because the Moon has no wind or rain, the footprints stay in the dust for a very long time.
asks: Why do Moon footprints stay put?

faq.a: Apollo 11 was the specific mission that successfully landed humans on the Moon in 1969.
asks: When did humans reach the Moon?
What mission landed people on the Moon?

facts: Rockets use powerful engines to travel through space.
Astronauts wear special suits to survive in space.
Apollo 11 landed humans on the Moon in 1969.
Footprints left on the Moon can stay visible for a long time.

quiz.say: What is needed to launch a rocket into space?
quiz.why: The engine creates the force needed to push the rocket up against Earth's gravity.

wrong.0: The astronauts are inside and they do not provide the main push.
wrong.1: Size alone does not create the necessary force for lift-off.
wrong.3: Gravity pulls things down, it does not push the rocket up.

quiz.say: What are astronauts trained to do?
quiz.why: Training prepares them for the unique environment of space travel.

wrong.0: They must learn about space, the Moon, and other planets too.
wrong.2: They must also train for living in the spacecraft itself.
wrong.3: While they know about them, their job is to travel in them.

quiz.say: What is the main evidence of human visits to the Moon?

options.show: A flag planted on the surface
options.say: A flag planted on the surface

quiz.why: These physical items show that people were actually there during the mission.

wrong.1: Pictures can be faked, but physical tracks are harder to fake.
wrong.2: There is no air on the Moon, so there is no sound to hear.
wrong.3: While flags were planted, the footprints are a more unique and lasting sign.
